one of three major open DFT databases alongside Materials Project and OQMD, enabling cross-database validation of property prediction models

reference database for thermodynamic convex hull stability — underpins most MLIP benchmarks for stability prediction

backbone dataset used to train CHGNet and MACE-MP universal potentials; covers 89 elements excluding noble gases and actinoids
provides comprehensive coverage of diverse chemical space with over 145,000 distinct compounds represented across the trajectory frames

uses PBE functional; particularly strong coverage of binary and ternary compounds for phase diagram and stability benchmarking
frequently used alongside Materials Project for benchmarking stability prediction and formation energy models

defines reproducible DFT parameter sets — k-point density, smearing, convergence thresholds, DFT+U for d/f-block elements — ensuring cross-material comparability
uses standardized Brillouin zone k-point paths for band structure calculations, enabling systematic electronic structure comparison across materials
dataset of ~175,000 stable and metastable inorganic crystals (within 100 meV/atom of the convex hull) computed with PBEsol and SCAN functionals using VASP (PAW, forces converged to 5 meV/Å)
tabulated properties include total energies, volumes, band gaps, total magnetic moments, and stress tensor components from both PBEsol and SCAN, enabling functional-comparison benchmarking
designed for training ML models for solid-state property prediction; freely available on the Materials Cloud repository as pymatgen-compatible ComputedStructureEntry JSON files

all calculations use VASP with PAW-PBE functional at 520 eV cutoff, Materials Project workflow DFT+U corrections for select transition metals, and a two-stage relaxation + static calculation protocol

stable compounds are annotated with band gaps, magnetic moments, and hardness; dataset publicly deposited and used to evaluate the generalization of universal MLIPs to unseen chemical space
